title: The Omnipotence of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The omnipotence of God means that God has all power to accomplish His holy will. Nothing is too hard for Him, and no creature, kingdom, sin, suffering, or spiritual power can overpower Him.
summary: The omnipotence of God means that God has all power to accomplish His holy will. Nothing is too hard for Him, and no creature, kingdom, sin, suffering, or spiritual power can overpower Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ displays divine power over creation, sickness, demons, sin, death, and the grave. The risen Lord has all authority and power to save, keep, raise, and restore His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is almighty. He made the heavens and the earth by His power, and no purpose of His can be stopped. His power is not limited by weakness, fear, opposition, or lack of resources.

God’s omnipotence is always holy and wise. He cannot deny Himself, lie, sin, or act against His own character. His power is not random force; it is the power of the righteous Lord.

Scripture repeatedly brings impossible situations before God. Barren wombs, enslaved people, mighty enemies, hardened sinners, and death itself are not beyond His power. What is impossible with man is possible with God.

Christ’s resurrection is the great display of saving power. God’s power is not only seen in creation, but in redemption, new birth, sanctification, perseverance, and final resurrection.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Weakness often makes people believe nothing can change. Sin feels too strong, suffering too long, enemies too powerful, and death too final. The omnipotence of God gives believers hope beyond human possibility.

This doctrine does not promise that God will do everything people desire on their timetable. It promises something better: the Almighty God can accomplish all His holy will, and He is strong enough to keep every promise in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring impossible things to God with faith and surrender. Do not measure God’s power by your strength, resources, or visible circumstances. Pray boldly, obey faithfully, and trust the Almighty Lord whose power is made known in Christ.
